filtersOrSort: None forwarded to the API. HomeFeed.tsx maintains a client-only `tab` state (for-you|following|trending) that is NEVER passed as a parameter to getFeed() — the same unfiltered call fires once on mount regardless of tab.
'following' tab: no API call is made at all for this tab; the UI unconditionally renders a hardcoded EmptyState ('Worth following' / 'Browse creators') irrespective of whatever `items` holds.

'trending' tab: renders the exact same `feed` array as 'for-you' with no distinct sort/filter applied — there is no trending-specific field (e.g. trending score) in ContentPiece and no separate endpoint call.
reads.pagination: None. Single unpaginated fetch of the full array on mount (useEffect with empty deps). No infinite scroll, no 'load more' control, no page/cursor param in getFeed().

authContext.notes: SessionGate.tsx (client component at '/') calls useSession().isAuthenticated and renders HomeFeed only when true; signed-out users see the passed-through landing `children` instead. No creatorGates() or account-type/role check is made anywhere in HomeFeed.tsx or SessionGate.tsx — the feed is identical for any authenticated user regardless of account type (user vs creator) or subscription/KYC state.

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: items === null, i.e. before the getFeed() promise settles (initial render through first effect tick)
the getFeed() promise passed to .then/.catch in HomeFeed rejects, setting error to a fixed string
uiStatesHandled.reachable: no — content.ts's getFeed() wraps its own apiFetch call in a try/catch and ALWAYS falls back to mockContent on any failure (mock-mode: apiFetch throws MockModeError immediately and is caught; the fallback itself has no external dependency and cannot fail). getFeed() therefore never rejects today, so HomeFeed's own .catch()/error branch is currently dead code. This remains true even once a real API_BASE is wired up, since the same try/catch would still swallow a real network failure and silently return mock data instead of surfacing the error UI — a gap worth flagging for backend/frontend reconciliation.

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: tab === 'following' (any time the user taps the Following tab)
uiStatesHandled.reachable: yes, but not data-driven — this branch is unconditional on `tab`, checked before the real `feed.length === 0` check, so it renders the same static EmptyState regardless of what getFeed() actually returned or whether the user follows anyone. There is no following-specific fetch or field (e.g. followedCreatorIds) anywhere in this screen's data layer.

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: tab !== 'following' && items !== null && error === null && feed.length === 0
uiStatesHandled.reachable: no — mockContent always contains 10 items and getFeed() unconditionally maps over the full array, so feed.length is never 0 under the current mock-driven app. Only reachable once a real backend can legitimately return an empty items array.

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: tab !== 'following' && items !== null && error === null && feed.length > 0

uiStatesDesigned.description: Default loaded feed: full-width ContentCard per item with an author row (avatar, name, VerificationBadge, relative time, overflow menu) above each card, locked and free cards shown back to back. Accompanying panel: 'One card, six treatments' — the same ContentCard in locked/free/unlocked states across all six content types (video, course, audio, pdf/post, image, template).
Skeleton row + skeleton card + a second skeleton row, no tab bar shown yet, header search bar only.

uiStatesDesigned.frame: 4 · Empty — following nobody, with a way out
uiStatesDesigned.description: Following tab: EmptyState ('You are not following anyone yet' / 'Follow a creator and their new work shows up here first' / action 'Find creators') PLUS a 'Worth following' section below it listing concrete suggested creators as ListRows (name, headline, location, a 'Follow' affordance) — the implementation only renders the bare EmptyState with a generic caption and 'Browse creators' action; it has no suggested-creators list at all.

uiStatesDesigned.frame: 5 · Browse — category, price and type filters
uiStatesDesigned.description: A distinct 'Browse' screen (back chevron + filters icon) with scrollable category chips (Business/Agriculture/Finance/Trade), a second row of active filter chips (Free/Under ₦1,000/Course/Video), a result-count line ('Business · Free · 38 pieces') with a Clear action, and a 2-column ContentCard grid. Not implemented anywhere in HomeFeed.tsx/content.ts — no category, price, or type filter state, no result-count field, and no distinct browse route exists in this screen's code.
